subject: ESEM model stops working once covariates are included (sex and race)

messages.author: 7ebd9b3a9eb36c58
messages.subject: ESEM model stops working once covariates are included (sex and race)
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I am using the sem.mi function to fit an ESEM model to 30 imputed datasets (imputed beforehand using Amelia, because I wanted to include specific auxiliary variables related to my research question in the imputation model). My sample size is 11,876. 

I have 18 binary indicators which I specified to be fit with an EFA of 3 latent factors, and I have 2 continuous endogenous variables which are regressed on the 3 latent factors. Since my data is categorical, I declared them as ordered and specified the WLSMV estimator. This model worked (and according to the fit indices, was of good fit) until I included two covariates (sex and race), then the model failed to run and produced the following error:

Error in .local(object, ...) : No imputations meet "omit.imps" criteria.

Both covariates were dummy coded as binary exogenous variables: Female_sex (recoded as female = 1 and male = 0) and five race categories with White as the reference level (e.g., recoded as American Indian = 1 and all other races = 0, then Asian = 1 and all other races = 0, etc.).

Here is my code (note: my data is a.out$imputations to access the imputed datasets from the Amelia object). I am using the 0.6-12 version of lavaan and the 0.5-6 version of semTools.

esemf3_cov <- '
# EFA
efa("efa")*f1 +
efa("efa")*f2 +
efa("efa")*f3 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10 + x11 + x12 + x13 + x14 + x15 + x16 + x17 + x18
# Regressions
y1 ~ f1 + f2 + f3 + Female_sex + American_Indian + Asian + Black + Native_Hawaiian + Other
y2 ~ f1 + f2 + f3 + Female_sex + American_Indian + Asian + Black + Native_Hawaiian + Other
'

imp_esemf3_cov <- sem.mi(esemf3_cov, data=a.out$imputations,
                     rotation = "oblimin", estimator = "WLSMV",
                     ordered = c("x1","x2", "x3", "x4",
                        "x5","x6", "x7", "x8",
                        "x9", "x10", "x11",
                        "x12", "x13", "x14",
                        "x15", "x16", "x17", "x18"))

To try to gain more insight into this error, I fit a SEM model to just one of the imputed datasets and received the following warning messages:

imp_esemf3_cov <- sem(esemf3_cov, data=a.out$imputations$imp1,
                     rotation = "oblimin", estimator = "WLSMV",
                     ordered = c("x1","x2", "x3", "x4",
                        "x5","x6", "x7", "x8",
                        "x9", "x10", "x11",
                        "x12", "x13", "x14",
                        "x15", "x16", "x17", "x18"))

Warning messages:
1: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = esemf3_multi_cov, data = a.out_ABCD$imputations$imp1,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    the optimizer (NLMINB) claimed the model converged, but not all
    elements of the gradient are (near) zero; the optimizer may not
    have found a local solution use check.gradient = FALSE to skip
    this check.
3: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic

4: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel.new, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
    (= 8.528232e-18) is close to zero. This may be a symptom that the
    model is not identified.

The most similar problem I could find in the discussion group archives was this 2020 thread which recommended changing my estimator to ML since my endogenous variables are continuous, but after I used ML the following error appeared:

imp_esemf3_cov <- sem(esemf3_cov, data=a.out$imputations$imp1,
                     rotation = "oblimin", estimator = "ML")

Error in (function (cond)  :
  error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'logLik': subscript out of bounds

I'm confused as to why my ESEM model can't run once covariates are included, when the same model without covariates runs perfectly fine.

Also, I have a theoretical question: are my three latent factors (f1, f2, f3) considered to be binary (like the indicators that make up each factor) or continuous exogenous variables? I'm unclear about what happens when each endogenous variable is regressed onto each latent factor - is each latent factor treated as a continuous factor score?

I would really appreciate your advice on this. Thank you in advance!

Best wishes,
Athena
